newsitem.title: JAPAN: Police estimate Japan has 80,000 "yakuza" mobsters.
newsitem.headline: Police estimate Japan has 80,000 "yakuza" mobsters.

text.p: The number of "yakuza" mobsters in Japan stood at 79,900 at the end of 1996, the National Police Agency (NPA) said in an annual estimate released on Thursday.
The figure, which includes full members and associates of organised crime groups, represents an increase of 600 over the previous year's estimate, the police said.
Japan's three largest criminal organisations -- the Yamaguchi-Gumi, the Inagawa-Kai and Sumiyoshi-Kai, respectively -- accounted for two-thirds of yakuza members and associates, the police said.
Yakuza, easily recognised by their colourful tattoos, fancy suits and tightly permed hair, have a long tradition in Japan. They are heavily involved in prostitution, gambling and extortion.
Continuing a crackdown which began with the strengthening of anti-mob laws in 1992, last year police took legal action against 33,270 mobsters and disbanded 218 mob groups, the NPA said.
